# llms.txt — HomeGeneratorGuide.com
# Independent standby-generator education for US homeowners. Not affiliated with any manufacturer.

## Core guides
- [Generator Sizing Guide](https://homegeneratorguide.com/sizing/what-size-generator-do-i-need/): Running vs starting watts, worked example, 10–26 kW ranges. Size by loads, never square footage alone.
- [Appliance Wattage Chart](https://homegeneratorguide.com/sizing/appliance-wattage-chart/): Running and starting watts for 28 common appliances.
- [Standby Generator Cost (2026)](https://homegeneratorguide.com/cost/standby-generator-cost/): $9,000–$16,000 installed typical; unit prices by model; line-item anatomy.
- [Generac vs Kohler](https://homegeneratorguide.com/comparisons/generac-vs-kohler/): Neutral criteria comparison with situation-based verdicts.
- [Generac Brand Review](https://homegeneratorguide.com/brands/generac/): Next Generation MSRP, tiered warranty, noise ratings, maintenance intervals.
- [Maintenance Checklist](https://homegeneratorguide.com/maintenance/generator-maintenance-checklist/): Owner vs pro tasks, brand intervals, battery testing, storm prep.

## Key facts (planning estimates — verify nameplates and get licensed quotes)
- Most single-family homes: 18–26 kW standby; essentials-only: 10–14 kW.
- Installed: $9,000–$16,000 typical single-family; 22 kW install labor $2,000–$5,000.
- Standby THD <5% (safe for home electronics); portables run 8–25%+.
- Standby CO risk is far lower than portable but nonzero — detectors on every level.
- No federal tax credit for standard standby generators.
